claims.text: The starting composite contains 67.5 wt.% CoCrFeNiMo0.2 matrix powder, 12.5 wt.% Ni-coated MoS2, 15 wt.% Ag, and 5 wt.% Cr2O3.
The powder mixture is uniformly ball-milled and subsequently consolidated by spark plasma sintering.
The intervention is to increase the HEA-matrix Mo content from x = 0.2 to x = 1 while retaining the other composite constituents.
Increasing Mo from x = 0.2 to x = 1 increases FCC lattice distortion.
Increasing Mo from x = 0.2 to x = 1 promotes formation of a hard, Mo-rich tetragonal sigma phase.
Ag, Ni/MoS2, and Cr2O3 remain at matrix boundaries after processing.
At lower temperatures, additional Mo provides solid-solution and second-phase strengthening.
Mo-induced strengthening suppresses plastic deformation and scratching during low-temperature sliding.
At high temperatures, Mo promotes tribochemical formation of layered silver molybdates and oxides.
Compaction of the tribochemical products forms a dense, continuous oxide-molybdate glaze.
The oxide-molybdate glaze separates the sliding surfaces and reduces interfacial shear.
The Mo1 composite will have lower friction and wear than the Mo0.2 composite across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
At 800 °C, the Mo1 composite will exhibit better wear resistance and a more robust, continuous glaze than the Mo0.2 composite.
The Mo0.2 baseline is predominantly an FCC solid solution with minimal sigma phase.
The Mo0.2 baseline has a friction coefficient of approximately 0.66 at room temperature, approximately 0.75 at 200 °C, and approximately 0.21 at 800 °C.
The Mo0.2 baseline has a wear rate of 13.1×10^-6 mm³/N·m at room temperature and 98.1×10^-6 mm³/N·m at 400 °C.
The proposed comparison is bounded to dry sliding in air against a 6 mm Si3N4 ball at 8 N, 0.15 m/s, a 4 mm rotation radius, and 270 m sliding distance from room temperature to 800 °C.
Tribological results may differ under other environments, counterfaces, loads, speeds, or sliding distances.
